title: RunEvent@1 envelope
description: The source of truth. One kernel sequencer allocates a monotonic per-run sequence while many reviewers execute concurrently. Events are never edited: a correction is a new compensating event. Large values live in content-addressed artifacts referenced by digest, never inline.

sequence.description: Monotonic per-run sequence allocated by the single sequencer. Dense and gapless: a gap means loss, not reordering.

type.description: Event type and semantic version, e.g. FindingReported@1. The vocabulary is closed by design — it is fixed in the phase that defines each event's payload, alongside the event store. Until then this is shape-checked, not enumerated, so the schema cannot lie about being complete.

occurred_at.description: Wall-clock observation, for humans and forensics. NOT an ordering authority — `sequence` is. Replay must never depend on this field.

causation_id.description: The event this one was caused by. Absent for a run's first event.

correlation_id.description: Subject this event is about across its lifetime, e.g. a Finding ID.

payload.description: Type-specific body. Must satisfy the I-JSON numeric domain: finite binary64, integers only within the interoperable safe range, no negative zero.
